cohort_summary: Gaze capture for all four learners falls far short of their matched experts. Active clinical focus was 0.0% (user0), 11.8% (user1), 7.1% (user2) and 4.4% (user3), against 91–94% for the ideal users. Recorded sessions for user1–user3 ran 13,558–15,815 s versus roughly 1,800 s for the experts, and user0's recording ended at 99 s. The learners' gaze is a sparse series of 1-second glances separated by long null gaps, plus a few very long fixations on non-clinical objects (bed hardware, ThermometerSnap2). Instructors should confirm whether these sessions were left running or had tracking problems before drawing firm conclusions about individual clinical reasoning. Each ideal user also modeled a different workflow: chest exam and cap refill for idealUser0, monitor surveillance for idealUser1, IV/med line/blood draw for idealUser2, and CodeSheet8kg/PenLight/iStat for idealUser3.

user2.recommended_next_focus: Take the first 60–90 seconds to establish perfusion and pulse (CaprefillChest, pulse), a monitor read, and the dose reference (CodeSheet), then start IV/med line tasks without long pauses. Practice quick, purposeful checks of Epinephrine_100_ and the CodeSheet before drawing or giving anything.
